description:
Ninja Creami Deluxe Teardown and Repair | Step-by-Step Fix Guide

In this video, I tear down and repair a Ninja Creami Deluxe ice cream maker! 🛠️ If your Ninja Creami isn’t working properly—whether it has no power cable, making strange noises, or the blade falls off—this step-by-step guide will help you troubleshoot and fix the problem.

You’ll learn how to:
 • Safely disassemble the Ninja Creami Deluxe
 • Identify and diagnose a common issue
 • Clean, repair, and reassemble the machine

Whether you’re an ice cream enthusiast or just trying to save money on repairs, this video covers everything you need to know to get your Ninja Creami Deluxe back in action! Don’t forget to like, subscribe, and hit the bell icon for more DIY appliance repairs and ice cream maker tips. 🍦🔧

If this video helps you repair your Ninja Creami Deluxe, let me know in the comments below! Also, share any tips or experiences you’ve had fixing appliances. 😊

The replacement dasher to buy: https://www.amazon.ca/dp/B0D9JDH8MH?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_fed_asin_title&th=1 (not an affiliate link btw)

The Ultimate Chocolate Recipe for you: https://youtu.be/u5hYG3yjZ0I?si=nDNzaCN7tVb-7y29&t=86 ✌️

-------------

⏱️ Timestamps:
0:00 - Intro
1:00 - Disassembling the Ninja Creami Deluxe
2:18 Cleaning the Ninja Creami Lid

comments.text: I just drilled out the magnet on the end of the NC-501 shaft.  It took a while and required a titanium carbide 0.125 drill bit and end mill in my dremel along with frequent drops of oil to manage the heat.  The magnet cavity measures 5 mm in diameter x 8 mm deep.  I just ordered a high temp N52 replacement from KJ Magnetics (D34-N52SH) its bit undersize, but has a 2.44 lb. pull strength and a temp rating up to 150 C which should solve the demag problem.  Most of the replacements are only good to 80 C.  I had to remove the elevator for the lid/jar assembly to get straight line access through the base.  You need tamper-proof socket drivers to get the screws out.  I update after I install the magnets and reassemble the unit.

Please Upvote! I tried 5x2, it worked but I cleaned the drill tip and blade with Qtips after, both had metal dust and the magnet had been chipped after one use.

I 3d printed two tiny 7x 0.25 mm disc's with TPU to sandwich the magnet which fixed the problem. The magnet worked without being chipped. If you dont have a 3d printer use silicone. I tested with ear plugs that I cut first but didn't know if they were bpa free so used my 3d printer.  

I was also able to get the blade on with the original magnet only by installing the pint with the machine upside down then flipping it lol. I didn't run it like this though as I read some people's blades fall off during use.

​@PolarIceCreamery Jaja I am, I was going to call it the Stranger Things technique but forgot while I was typing. Some new findings,
-I'm using 7.5 x 0.25 mm top and bottom. Would probably be more durable around 0.35 mm but someone commented 5x3 mm made their machine scratch the pint. Also nothing wrong with these 0.25mm just thinking.
- The 7.5 mm on the top part for the drill might be better perfectly fitted around 7. I want it completely covering the magnet from the drill edges but installing the Creami feels stiffer now so I might be rubbing the TPU agaisnt the blade insert. The bottom fits perfectly though and 0.25mm doesn't cover the hole.
-You could probably super glue tpu to the magnet but I just take them all out separately. Quickly shove disc in the blade and use a wooden stir to press it in place. Then use my fingers to line up the drill TPU and let the magnet hold it in place.
-Had 2 microchips on a magnet after Lite Ice Cream. No issues with normal.

comments.text: I just drilled out the magnet on the end of the NC-501 shaft.  It took a while and required a titanium carbide 0.125 drill bit and end mill in my dremel along with frequent drops of oil to manage the heat.  The magnet cavity measures 5 mm in diameter x 8 mm deep.  I just ordered a high temp N52 replacement from KJ Magnetics (D34-N52SH) its bit undersize, but has a 2.44 lb. pull strength and a temp rating up to 150 C which should solve the demag problem.  Most of the replacements are only good to 80 C.  I had to remove the elevator for the lid/jar assembly to get straight line access through the base.  You need tamper-proof socket drivers to get the screws out.  I update after I install the magnets and reassemble the unit.

comments.text:
Thank you for this interesting video !
However Please consider this : the motorspindle has an auger type formed thread which causes the paddle knife  not to disengage from the shaft when it is rotating down and up . The original magnet which holds the paddle knife connected to the spindle is  countersunk in the spindle to form a flat surface  and a sort of flange , so the paddle knife rests on that flange when fully engaged. On putting an extra 2 mm magnet in the paddle knife or on top of the spindle shaft there is a gap between the spindle flange and the paddle knife. The magnet is in that case  absorbing a lot of the force exceeded when the spindle is rotating down. So it might be preferred to drill the old magnet out of the spindle or to carefully observe the piggybacked magnets condition after each spin. Drilling out the magnet is “ quite a task “ and “ challenge “ . I did it with a Dremel and a small diamond bur and did not glue the new magnet because it holds itself .

​ @Mark-ks9jj  but haven't you thought about tiny layers of food getting inside the housing during operation as the shaft goes up and down and causing growth of micro organisms?
 The inside also is quite bad - the main shaft's bearing (which is just above the blade), lubrication can spill out into the food (have seen that). Also, the electronics suspend all kinds of atoms from the pcb & chips onto the shaft and the food. The shaft is not isolated from any of these.

The rubber seal cannot get 100% of the food while the shaft moves up and down. 

Have groove where the blades get on also seem to demagnetise and fall off after frequent usage (magents to hold the blades intially - super design).
The grooves (which should provide the blades with cetrifugal engagemnet during operation rather than the magnets when stationary), also seem to wear off.

Very poor design health wise, sustainabilkity wise, etc.

One has to buy a whole new product from them when any of these happen.
As a electronics, virologist, just cannot ignore these hazards and children want to use it frequently.

The same seems to be the case with other product lines they manufacture.. things wear off, then people buy again - sales for them, and give no fk about health concerns.

But looks like many just don't care or are ignorant or so.
Either way thanks for the reply. ciao
